RESOLUTION NO. 24 OF 2021

A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR AND CITY
CLERK~TREASURER TO ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH
WOOSTER CONSTRUCTION CO., LLC FOR MOUNTAIN SPRINGS
DRAINAGE IMPROVEMENTS; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the City of Cabot is in need of drainage improvements along the north
side of Mountain Springs Road; and

WHEREAS, the City engaged in competitive bidding under the applicable provisions of
state and local law, and Wooster Construction Co., LLC returned the lowest responsible bid for
the services the City was seeking; and

WHEREAS, the City desires to enter into an agreement with Wooster Construction
Co., LLC for drainage improvements along Mountain Springs Road which is further
delineated on Exhibit “A” attached hereto and incorporated herein by this reference.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION 1: The Mayor and City Clerk~Treasurer are hereby authorized to enter
in an agreement with Wooster Construction Co., LLC for drainage improvements along
Mountain Springs Road in the amount of $129,022.00. The approved agreement shall be

consistent with the terms in the attached Exhibit A.

SECTION 2: This resolution shall be in full force and effect from and after its

passage.

April 26, 2021

To: Cabot City Council

From: Joe Gunderman - Director of Street & Infrastructure

Re: Mt. Springs Drainage Project

Dear Council Members;

On April 13, 2021, the City had a bid opening for the Mt. Springs Drainage Project with five (5)
prospective bidders.

As you will see by the enclosed bid tabulation, Site Work One submitted the lowest bid of $122,264.00.
However, the bidder did not acknowledge the two addenda, which was required within the bid
documents. After consulting with City Attorney Ben Hooper, it was determined that the bid provided by
Site Work One was disqualified because of this fact.

The next lowest bid was submitted by Wooster Construction Co., LLC for $129,022.00. The bid submitted
by Wooster Construction Co., LLC did meet all of the requirements of the bid documents, making them
the lowest qualified bidder.

If you have any questions, please feel free to ask.

Scope of Services/Work

Since Federal funds will be used for the Project, an environmental review and appropriate
documentation is required in accordance with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), 23

Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 771, and ARDOT requirements. This scope of work and

fee estimate are based on the assumption that the proposed improvements would meet the

requirements of 23 CFR 771.117, Categorical Exclusions. The Project is assumed to be

considered a “c-list” CE project based on 23 CFR 771.117(c)(3) construction of bicycle and pedestrian
lanes, paths, and facilities. In the event it is determined by ARDOT or the Federal Highway
Administration (FHWA) that a CE is not the appropriate level of documentation for the Project,
Consultant will notify the Owner and a supplemental scope of work will be prepared to allow completion
of other suitable documentation.

The following tasks will be necessary to receive a CE determination from ARDOT:

A. Project Scoping

Consultant will perform project scoping in coordination with ARDOT and the City of Cabot to initiate
the CE determination process. This task includes one meeting with the Owner and/or ARDOT, if
necessary.

B. Data Collection and Environmental Constraints Mapping

Consultant will obtain digital environmental information available from appropriate local, state,
and federal agencies. Data collected through this task will be stored in Geographical Information
Systems (GIS) format. Consultant will perform a site visit of the Project area to document
existing conditions. This task includes taking on-site photographs. It is assumed the Project
corridor is accessible and right of entry from private property owners will not be necessary.

C. Natural and Physical Environment

Review protected species lists from the Arkansas Natural Heritage Commission (ANHC) and the
United States Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) for Lonoke County. Conclusions will be
made, based on general observations from a visual survey and the literature review, regarding
whether preferred habitat or designated critical habitat for any listed threatened and endangered
species is present within the Project area, whether any listed species is likely to occur, and
whether there is a potential impact or effect to listed species.

A jurisdictional determination of waters of the United States, including wetlands, will be made
within the anticipated ROW and areas anticipated to be disturbed by construction for the Project.
This determination will include delineation of the boundaries and ordinary high-water mark of
jurisdictional waters within the Project area.

Document floodplains, aquifers, navigable waters, and state or federal scenic rivers within the
Project area.

Determine farmland impacts. Identification of farmland impacts shall be in accordance with the
Farmland Protection Policy Act (FPPA) (7 USC 4201 et. seq.) and guidance on addressing FPPA
requirements, which includes determining whether the project is exempt or completion of form
AD 1006 or CPA 106 as appropriate.

Identify any hazardous waste sites, leaking underground storage tanks, oil/gas wells, or other
potentially contaminated sites in the Project area. This task will include review of environmental
regulatory databases and visual observations of the Project site.

U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Natural Resources Conservation Commission (NRCS),

Item No. 3 - Streetscape Phase III Project
CITY OF CABOT
MAIN STREET / HWY. 89 STREETSCAPE - PHASE III
Scope of Services/Work
Since Federal funds will be used for the Project, an environmental review and appropriate
documentation is required in accordance with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), 23
Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 771, and ARDOT requirements. This scope of work and
fee estimate are based on the assumption that the proposed improvements would meet the
requirements of 23 CFR 771.117, Categorical Exclusions. The Project is assumed to be
considered a “c-list” CE project based on 23 CFR 771.117(c)(3) construction of bicycle and pedestrian
lanes, paths, and facilities. In the event it is determined by ARDOT or the Federal Highway
Administration (FHWA) that a CE is not the appropriate level of documentation for the Project,
Consultant will notify the Owner and a supplemental scope of work will be prepared to allow completion
of other suitable documentation.
The following tasks will be necessary to receive a CE determination from ARDOT:
A. Project Scoping
Consultant will perform project scoping in coordination with ARDOT and the City of Cabot to initiate
the CE determination process. This task includes one meeting with the Owner and/or ARDOT, if
necessary.
B. Data Collection and Environmental Constraints Mapping
Consultant will obtain digital environmental information available from appropriate local, state,
and federal agencies. Data collected through this task will be stored in Geographical Information
Systems (GIS) format. Consultant will perform a site visit of the Project area to document
existing conditions. This task includes taking on-site photographs. It is assumed the Project
corridor is accessible and right of entry from private property owners will not be necessary.
C. Natural and Physical Environment
Review protected species lists from the Arkansas Natural Heritage Commission (ANHC) and the
United States Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) for Lonoke County. Conclusions will be
made, based on general observations from a visual survey and the literature review, regarding
whether preferred habitat or designated critical habitat for any listed threatened and endangered
species is present within the Project area, whether any listed species is likely to occur, and
whether there is a potential impact or effect to listed species.
A jurisdictional determination of waters of the United States, including wetlands, will be made
within the anticipated ROW and areas anticipated to be disturbed by construction for the Project.
This determination will include delineation of the boundaries and ordinary high-water mark of
jurisdictional waters within the Project area.
Document floodplains, aquifers, navigable waters, and state or federal scenic rivers within the
Project area.
Determine farmland impacts. Identification of farmland impacts shall be in accordance with the
Farmland Protection Policy Act (FPPA) (7 USC 4201 et. seq.) and guidance on addressing FPPA
requirements, which includes determining whether the project is exempt or completion of form
AD 1006 or CPA 106 as appropriate.
Identify any hazardous waste sites, leaking underground storage tanks, oil/gas wells, or other
potentially contaminated sites in the Project area. This task will include review of environmental
regulatory databases and visual observations of the Project site.

CITY OF CABOT
MAIN STREET / HWY. 89 STREETSCAPE - PHASE III
D. Cultural Resources
Identify cultural resources in the Project area in compliance with the requirements of Section 106
of the National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA) [16 USC § 470(f)] and implementing
regulations (36 CFR Part 800). A records review will be conducted to identify recorded
archeological or historic sites within the area of potential effects (APE) for the Project.
E. Socioeconomics
Document public service facilities and community resources such as parks, medical facilities,
churches and schools adjacent to the Project. Document the population and income characteristics
of the Project area, and identify potential Environmental Justice (EJ) and Limited English

TRANSPORTATION ALTERNATIVES PROGRAM (TAP)

PROJECT APPLICATION -- FFY 2021

The Transportation Alternatives Program provides funding for programs and projects
defined as transportation alternatives, including on and off road pedestrian and bicycle
facilities, infrastructure projects for improving non-driver access to public transportation
and enhanced mobility, community improvement activities and environmental
mitigation; safe routes to school projects; and projects or construction of boulevards
and other roadways largely in the right-of-way of former Interstate System routes or
other divided highways. Agencies of city, county, state or federal government and duly
incorporated private/non-profit agencies, who partner with local public agencies (LPAs),
can apply for these funds if access to the project by the general public is provided
throughout the life of the project.

A local sponsor must provide at least 20% of the eligible project costs. Federal funds
from other sources cannot be used to match these funds. This is a reimbursable
program, which means once the sponsor receives an official Notice to Proceed from the
Arkansas Department of Transportation (ARDOT), up to 80% of the costs directly
attributable to the construction of the project can be reimbursed. The local sponsor is
responsible for maintaining records and proving that expenses are legitimate and
directly related to the project. This may be in the form of receipts, time sheets, etc.

submitted with the application. A draft resolution should have been downloaded with

WHEREAS, Ark. Code Ann § 14-42-107(b)(1) states that no alderman, council member,
official, or municipal employee shall be interested, directly or indirectly, in the profit of any
contract for furnishing supplies, equipment, or services to the municipality unless the governing
body of the city has enacted an ordinance specifically permitting alderman, council members,
officials, or municipal employees to conduct business with the city; and

WHEREAS, the City of Cabot is in need of 4WD Regular Cab Dump Truck with 3.5
to 5 yard Dump Bed; and

WHEREAS, the City engaged in competitive bidding under the applicable provisions of
state and local law, and Red River Dodge returned the lowest sealed bid for the vehicle the City
was seeking; and

WHEREAS, Mitch Ward is a commissioner on the Cabot Planning Commission. He is
also the owner of Red River Dodge, which provided the lowest sealed bid for the vehicle in
question; and

WHEREAS, the City desires to enter into an agreement with Red River Dodge for a

4WD Regular Cab Dump Truck which is further delineated on Exhibit “A” attached hereto and
incorporated herein by this reference.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: Mitch Ward, as owner of Red River Dodge, is hereby permitted to
conduct business with the City of Cabot, Arkansas by providing the vehicle referenced herein in
accordance with the sealed bid submitted by Red River Dodge.

SECTION 2: The Mayor and City Clerk~Treasurer are hereby authorized to enter in

to an agreement with Red River Dodge for a4WD Regular Cab Dump Truck in the amount

May 18, 2021
PRESENT: Jay Lallu, Candace Tomboli, Stephen Redd, Bryan Knowles, Matt Webber, Greg Jones & Bryan

GUESTS PRESENT: Travis Young with Parks & Rec., Clint McGue, legal counsel, Sarah Brown, & Gina Jones, all with

Jay Lallu called the meeting to order at 8:27 am
Pledge: Jay Lallu

Gina Jones gave roll call.
Minutes- The Commissioners reviewed the minutes from the April 2021 meeting Motion to approve was made by
Bryan Knowles with Stephen Redd making the second. The commission voted and the April 2021 minutes were
approved.
Financial Report - The Commission reviewed the April 2021 financial report. Bryan Knowles made a motion to
approve the financial report, Greg Jones made the second, the financial report for April 2021 was approved.
Funding Requests:
Cabot Chamber of Commerce – We were asking for $18,018.69 for the directory, printing, and mailing. Sarah Brown
spoke about the directory and how many people it would reach and talk about our city to draw people from all over to
our town. Matt Webber spoke that he had seen one at the rest stop in Corning and Jay Lallu said that he had seen one at
the rest stop in Lake Village, AR. Sarah talked about how this directory hits all the points for A&P funding. Jay said
that the Chamber would still make a profit with this and that if they gave us the money, that it would be nothing but
profit for us. Jay asked why we did not use Al Canelli for the directory anymore and it was explained to the
commission that we brought it in house to try and recoup lost revenue due to not having Cabotfest in 2020. Sarah did
explain that this directory would be a yearly thing, Bryan Knowles mentioned that this might be a yearly budgeted item.
Jay continued to say that this is a chamber publication and that he did not feel that it was a Cabot directory. Sarah told
him that it was in fact geared to Cabot, showcasing many different areas of Cabot that is mailed out to 10,000 plus
people. Greg Jones mentioned that maybe the A&P should just fund a portion of the amount requested. Greg said that
he could make a motion for a dollar amount and then it could be discussed as to how much to approve. Greg made a
motion to approve $3,000 of the $18,018 asked for, Candace Tomboli made a 2nd, and it was approved. There were no
more discussions.
Cabot Country Cruisers – Janie Smith was here to ask for a funding request for Family Track Nights, she said that the
A&P normally funds their Spring Fling and that did not happen due to COVID. They sponsor track nights every
Monday night, catering more to kids that cannot necessarily afford to play sports or gymnastics. We give shirts,
medals, water, and popsicles to all that participate. It is a fun thing for families to do together. They are asking for $750
to help to offset the costs. We have estimated our cost to be just over $1,700. In 2019 there was roughly 150 kids come
out. We are hoping for at least 200 this year. Bryan Knowles made the motion to approve the $750 request and Greg
Jones said that the A&P needed to be on the shirts and Stephen Redd made the 2nd all voted and it was approved.
Chamber Report – Sarah Brown mentioned that we have our golf tournament coming up on June 30th. We have the Ice
Cream Social that will be in July. We also are working on Cabotfest already. We had 5 new members and we currently
have two ribbon cutting coming up. One on June 1st for State Farm, Chas Tamburo and one on June 11th for Buff City
Soap.

36

Cabot Parks & Rec – Travis Young was here and said that they have a huge ball tournament in town this weekend
with 205 teams. We had so many, that they had to send some teams to Conway and that has never happened, and they
were not going to be able to have a tournament until we did this. They are also having a big Memorial Day softball
tournament as well and will have teams from all over the country. Our league stuff is going great. Flag football
finished up this past weekend. Because of the turf, we have been able to play some nights that nobody else could be due
to the weather. Since A&P paid to fix the mess ups at the aquatic park, he told us that the dive well has been re-coated,
and it looks great. The main pool, when we drained it, it had a crack in the bottom of it. We will hold off on coating
that until we can fix it, so it will be coated after Labor Day. We will also probably do our lazy river then as well. It will
make the whole park look brand new.
General Discussion – Jay Lallu mentioned that he has spoken to the Little Rock Chamber and the NLR Chamber and
they both recommend MUNIrevs to do the online A&P payments. They are out of Colorado. I have spoken to IDM
about doing a website for us and they would post the link to payments and it would send you to the MUNIrevs site and
you could continue to do your payment. The payments would go directly to their accounts in Quickbooks. It would be
$12,500 a year. $2,000 for the set up and a $10,000 hosting fee yearly. For IDM, there are two different options.
Option one would be $800 per phase or $2400 for all three phases listed, plus a yearly hosting fee of $175 and yearly
domain fee of $20. Option 2 would be $225 per month with a one time $500 upfront set up fee. Jay says that he feels
Option 1 is the best option for us. Jay asked if we need to proceed or wait until we talk to Bentonville to see if they use
someone differently? Greg said he would like for Jay to get some more information and discuss this again at the June
meeting.
Bryan Knowles commission expires on July 1, 2021. Bryan said that he would like to continue as a commissioner.

Clint said that he would do a resolution and submit it to the city.
Clint said that the delinquencies had been held up with code enforcement delivering the letters. He was waiting to hear
back from Ben Hooper. He feels that it will be worked out very soon.
Jay asked if the commission had a surety bond to protect the commissioners. Clint suggested that we check with the
city.
The next A&P meeting will be June 15, 2021.

AGENDA ITEMS
In response to the 2020 COVID-19 outbreak and restrictions placed on
social distancing by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot
moved the monthly Planning Commission Meeting to the Veterans Park
Event Center, 508 North Lincoln. This allowed for ten feet of spacing
between chairs as suggested. The meeting was both open to the public
and an online meeting with video through the web-based video
conferencing tool Zoom.
1. Call to Order
Chairman Young called to order the regular meeting of the Cabot
Planning Commission at 7:00 PM, at the Veterans Park Event Center.
Opening prayer and the Pledge of Allegiance were led by Commissioner
Young.
2. Roll Call
A roll call was conducted. The following persons were present:
Commission members Liz Bird, Chuck Prater, Ronny Loe, Claude Irvin,
Mitch Ward, Matt Moudy and Chairman Young and City Attorney Ben
Hooper, Halff – City Engineer Brian Vines. Present via Zoom was Garver –
City Planner Courtney McNair and Mayor Ken Kincade.
3. Approval of Minutes from Last Meeting and Other Matters
The minutes of the April 2021 Regular Planning Commission meeting
were approved with a motion by Mr. Prater and a second by Ms. Bird,
Motion passed unanimously by a Roll Call Vote.
4. Planning Commission (Public Hearing)
a) Rezone – 454 Diederich Lane from, R-1 to C-2 – (Mr. and Mrs.
Richard House)
After a brief discussion on downgrading the zoning request from C-2
to O-1 zoning, a Motion to approve zoning from R-1 to O-1 by Mr.
Moudy, second by Mr. Ward, motion was approved unanimously by
Roll Call Vote, 6-0-0 and is now passed to City Council.

5. Planning Commission (New Business)
a) Site Plan – Lot 1R, Cabot Commerce Center (Lemons Engineering)

39

After a brief discussion, a Motion to approve with contingencies by
Mr. Ward, second by Mr. Loe, motion was approved with
contingencies unanimously by Roll Call Vote, 5-0-1 with the following
contingencies: The proposed sidewalk along Jayden Commercial
Court must tie into the existing sidewalk at the landing and not at the
ramp on Arkansas State Highway 38; The drainage and grading need
to be updated to include the addition of the sidewalk along Jayden
Commercial Court; Cabot Waterworks requires a signed Developers
Agreement prior to construction of water and sewer facilities. Claude
Irvin abstained from voting.
b) Final Plat – Greystone Estates – (Lemons Engineering) After a
brief discussion, a Motion to approve with contingencies by Mr.
Prater, a second by Mr. Moudy motion was approved unanimously by
Roll Call Vote, 6-0-0 with the following contingencies: The sidewalk
along Corbin Circle must be replaced from the damage that occurred
on 5/5/2012; Provide recorded easement document for the off-site
utility easement on the sewer extension; Street lights must be
installed or a letter from the electric company stating their intent to
install street lights and when they intend to install them; The entire
street of sub-grade must be proof-rolled and pass density testing;
Curb and gutter and asphalt must be installed; Final Mandrel Test
and camera inspection on sewer mains must be done.
6.

Adjournment
There being no further business to come before the Planning
Commission, the meeting was adjourned at 7:48 p.m.

A RESOLUTION EXPRESSING THE WILLINGNESS OF THE CITY OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS TO UTILIZE FEDERAL-AID TRANSPORTATION ALTERNATIVES
PROGRAM FUNDS FOR THE UPDATED HIGHWAY 321 SIDEWALK PROJECT
WHEREAS, in Resolution 33 of 2021 the Cabot City Council previously approved
Cabot’s participation in the Highway 321 Sidewalk project in conjunction with the Arkansas
Department of Transportation; and
WHEREAS, the Highway 321 Sidewalk Project utilizes Federal Aid Transportation
Alternative Program Funds and involves those funds paying for 80% of the project and the City
of Cabot paying for the other 20%; and
WHEREAS, subsequent to the passage of Resolution 33 of 2021, the Arkansas
Department of Transportation has updated the Highway 321 Sidewalk Project to include
approximately an additional two miles on sidewalks along Highway 321; and
WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council wishes to support the City’s participation in the
updated Highway 321 Sidewalk Project. The City Council acknowledges that the Arkansas

Department of Transportation has estimated that the City’s 20% of the updated project is
approximately $56,400 and that these funds will be paid from the City’s Sidewalk Fund.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
CABOT, ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION I: The City of Cabot is hereby authorized to participate in the updated
Highway 321 Sidewalk project. The Mayor and the City Clerk~Treasurer are hereby authorized
to expend funds in the amount of $56,400 from the City’s Sidewalk Fund to pay for its
designated share of the program. The City Council understands and acknowledges that amount
is based off an estimate of the total project amount provided by the Arkansas Department of
Transportation and that if the estimate changes, the City’s share of participation may also
change.

SECTION II: The Mayor and City Clerk-Treasurer are hereby authorized and directed to
execute all appropriate agreements and contracts necessary to effectuate its participation in the
updated Highway 321 Sidewalk Project.

SECTION III: This resolution shall be in full force and effect from and after its passage.

ORDINANCE NO. 18 OF 2021

AN ORDINANCE CREATING, CERTIFYING, AND CONFIRMING TAX LIENS
AGAINST REAL PROPERTIES AT VARIOUS LOCATIONS WITHIN THE CITY OF
CABOT FOR FUNDS EXPENDED TO PAY FOR SERVICES RENDERED DUE TO
CODE VIOLATIONS; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, due to violations of the City of Cabot’s Code of Ordinances, the City has
expended funds for services rendered and/or performed by and/or on behalf of the City of Cabot
for certain work on real properties located within the city limits to remove/modify noncompliant
conditions. A list of the relevant real properties is attached hereto as Exhibit A.

WHEREAS, despite notice and demand, the property owners at issue have not paid the
amounts due to the City for services rendered and/or performed as detailed herein; and

WHEREAS, pursuant to Arkansas law, tax liens may and should be created and certified
for these real properties and record property owners as listed in Exhibit A. Furthermore, the lien
amounts should be certified for inclusion in the annual real estate tax statements prepared by the
Lonoke County Treasurer’s Office or other appropriate county office.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION 1: In accordance with the authority granted under A.C.A. 14-54-901 et seq.,
the Cabot City Council hereby authorizes the Mayor and/or the City Clerk~Treasurer to certify the
list of real properties and amounts due, plus ten percent, attached hereto to the Lonoke County
Circuit Clerk’s Office, Lonoke County Treasurer’s Office, and any other appropriate office for
inclusion as tax liens on the annual real property tax statements for 2021. A list of the relevant
real properties is attached as Exhibit A and is hereby incorporated into this ordinance by this
reference.

SECTION 2: In accordance with A.C.A 14-54-904, the liens authorized and confirmed
herein by the Cabot City Council may be enforced by the City for ten years. The ten-year period

of time commences upon the filing of the lien with the Lonoke County Circuit Clerk’s office.

WHEREAS, The City of Cabot and the Cabot Parks and Recreation Commission seek to
help improve the recreation facilities and wishes to seek grant funding assistance; and

WHEREAS, in order to obtain the funds necessary to develop and/or improve the site for
such a recreation area, it is necessary to obtain an Outdoor Recreation Matching Grant from the
Arkansas Department of Parks, Heritage and Tourism; and

WHEREAS, the plans for such recreation areas have been prepared and the price,
therefore, has been established; and

WHEREAS, this governing body understands the grantee and grantor will enter into a
binding agreement which obligates both parties to policies and procedures contained within the
Outdoor Recreation Matching Grant Application Guide, including, but not limited to the
following: the park area defined by the project boundary map, submitted with the application,
must remain in outdoor recreation use in perpetuity, regardless if the property is bought or
developed with matching grant funds and; all future overhead utility lines within the project
boundary must be placed underground and; the project area must remain open and available for
use by the public at all reasonable times of the day and year; facilities can be reserved for special
events, league play, etc. but cannot be reserved, leased or assigned for exclusive use, and; the
project area must be kept clean, maintained, and operated in a safe and healthful manner;

The Cabot City Council is well aware and apprised of the above-mentioned project, and
that the Cabot Parks and Recreation Commission will provide the local portion of the
development cost of the entire project.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
CABOT, ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION 1: The Mayor and City Clerk~Treasurer are hereby authorized to make
application to the Arkansas Department of Parks, Heritage and Tourism for assistance to develop
recreational facilities for the City and the Cabot Parks and Recreation Commission. The Mayor

and take any further action necessary to effectuate the City’s participation in the grant referenced

MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING (MOU)
BETWEEN
THE CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS
AND
CRISWELL-ROBINSON AMERICAN LEGION POST 71

SUBJECT: MOU

This MOU is between the City of Cabot, Arkansas and American Legion Post 71. When
referred to collectively, the City of Cabot and Criswell-Robinson American Legion Post 71
are referred to as the “Parties.”

1. BACKGROUND. The Criswell-Robinson Legion Post 71 is a Veteran Non-Profit
501c¢19 organization that works heavily in the Cabot community area for the Veterans
of the area, the Children and Youth, and Americanism as well. There are two primary
purposes of Criswell-Robinson American Legion Post 71. First is to support the
Lonoke County Veterans Service Office in assisting veterans and transitioning
servicemembers in filing claims for the many benefits available to them through the
Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). In this role, and in accordance with 38 U.S.C.
section 5902, American Legion Post 71 supports the Lonoke County Veteran’s
Service Officer who has been granted recognition in the preparation, presentation,
and prosecution of claims under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans
Affairs. The second purpose is to provide a means for honorable discharged veterans
to continue to support their communities and fellow citizens.

2. PURPOSE. This MOU addresses the responsibilities of each of the Parties incident
to the functioning of Criswell-Robinson American Legion Post 71 at the city provided
facility and the use of available space and associated services for the purpose of
providing VA-accredited representation services to servicemembers and support of
community activities. For purposes of this MOU, the term “associated services”
includes existing lighting, heating, cooling, electricity, water, sewage and Internet
services.

3. UNDERSTANDING OF THE PARTIES.
3.1 The City of Cabot will:

3.1.1. Provide American Legion Post 71 with access to the building located at 600 N.
Grant Street for the purpose of exclusive, full-time use of the building and parking area
for the sole purpose of providing VA-accredited representation services and Post 71
community support activities. The space provided will allow for private and confidential
conversations to take place between the accredited American Legion Post 71
representative and his/her servicemember client(s). Facility access and use of space will
be provided at no cost to American Legion Post 71.

MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING (MOU)
BETWEEN
THE CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS
AND
CRISWELL-ROBINSON AMERICAN LEGION POST 71
SUBJECT: MOU
This MOU is between the City of Cabot, Arkansas and American Legion Post 71. When
referred to collectively, the City of Cabot and Criswell-Robinson American Legion Post 71
are referred to as the “Parties.”
1. BACKGROUND. The Criswell-Robinson Legion Post 71 is a Veteran Non-Profit
501c19 organization that works heavily in the Cabot community area for the Veterans
of the area, the Children and Youth, and Americanism as well. There are two primary
purposes of Criswell-Robinson American Legion Post 71. First is to support the
Lonoke County Veterans Service Office in assisting veterans and transitioning
servicemembers in filing claims for the many benefits available to them through the
Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). In this role, and in accordance with 38 U.S.C.
section 5902, American Legion Post 71 supports the Lonoke County Veteran’s
Service Officer who has been granted recognition in the preparation, presentation,
and prosecution of claims under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans
Affairs. The second purpose is to provide a means for honorable discharged veterans
to continue to support their communities and fellow citizens.
2. PURPOSE. This MOU addresses the responsibilities of each of the Parties incident
to the functioning of Criswell-Robinson American Legion Post 71 at the city provided
facility and the use of available space and associated services for the purpose of
providing VA-accredited representation services to servicemembers and support of
community activities. For purposes of this MOU, the term “associated services”
includes existing lighting, heating, cooling, electricity, water, sewage and Internet
services.
3. UNDERSTANDING OF THE PARTIES.
3.1 The City of Cabot will:
3.1.1. Provide American Legion Post 71 with access to the building located at 600 N.
Grant Street for the purpose of exclusive, full-time use of the building and parking area
for the sole purpose of providing VA-accredited representation services and Post 71
community support activities. The space provided will allow for private and confidential
conversations to take place between the accredited American Legion Post 71
representative and his/her servicemember client(s). Facility access and use of space will
be provided at no cost to American Legion Post 71.

required for the delivery of VA-accredited representation services in the space provided
for that activity. Such associated services will be provided at no cost to American Legion
Post 71.
3.1.3. Appoint a representative to serve as the liaison between American Legion Post 71
and the City of Cabot to facilitate access to the installation and the provision of installation
space and associated services. The representative will:

3.1.3.5 The City of Cabot herein acknowledges and accepts the continued and

Post 71 to the Cabot Community as consideration for this agreement.
3.2. American Legion Post 71 will:

and the use of space and associated services under the provisions of this MOU are

Veterans Service Officer who is accredited by the VA for providing representation

under this MOU are to providing services to active duty, retired and separated Service
members who have requested them. Such services will be provided at no cost to Service

3.2.4. Agree to not use provided space and associated services for political or unAmerican activities. The American Legion is an apolitical organization charter by the

SUBJECT: MOU
This MOU is between the City of Cabot, Arkansas and American Legion Post 71. When
referred to collectively, the City of Cabot and Criswell-Robinson American Legion Post 71
are referred to as the “Parties.”
1. BACKGROUND. The Criswell-Robinson Legion Post 71 is a Veteran Non-Profit
501c19 organization that works heavily in the Cabot community area for the Veterans
of the area, the Children and Youth, and Americanism as well. There are two primary
purposes of Criswell-Robinson American Legion Post 71. First is to support the
Lonoke County Veterans Service Office in assisting veterans and transitioning
servicemembers in filing claims for the many benefits available to them through the
Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). In this role, and in accordance with 38 U.S.C.
section 5902, American Legion Post 71 supports the Lonoke County Veteran’s
Service Officer who has been granted recognition in the preparation, presentation,
and prosecution of claims under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans
Affairs. The second purpose is to provide a means for honorable discharged veterans
to continue to support their communities and fellow citizens.
2. PURPOSE. This MOU addresses the responsibilities of each of the Parties incident
to the functioning of Criswell-Robinson American Legion Post 71 at the city provided
facility and the use of available space and associated services for the purpose of
providing VA-accredited representation services to servicemembers and support of
community activities. For purposes of this MOU, the term “associated services”
includes existing lighting, heating, cooling, electricity, water, sewage and Internet
services.

Grant Street for the purpose of exclusive, full-time use of the building and parking area
for the sole purpose of providing VA-accredited representation services and Post 71
community support activities. The space provided will allow for private and confidential
conversations to take place between the accredited American Legion Post 71
representative and his/her servicemember client(s). Facility access and use of space will
be provided at no cost to American Legion Post 71.

Cabot City Council Work Session
Veterans Park Event Center
July 6, 2021
6:30 p.m.

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on social distancing
by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot moved the monthly Work Session
to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508 N. Lincoln, as advertised. This allowed for spacing
between chairs, as suggested. The event was successfully streamed through YouTube.
You may view this meeting at
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x_7QelAo15A&t=2942s.

Council members present were: Ed Long, Michael Jones, Brandon Hillenburg, Maggie
Cope, James Reid, Matt Webber, Ron Waymack and Stephen Redd. Others present:
Mayor Ken Kincade, City Attorney Ben Hooper, and City Clerk & Treasurer Tammy Yocom.

Mayor Kincade opened the meeting at 6:30 p.m.

Municipal Services Committee Business: (Members are: Long, Reid, Redd & Cope)
As Chairman, Ed Long opened this committee meeting by asking Matt Webber to
address the upcoming code amendments regarding food trucks. Matt explained he would
like to gather feedback on the highlighted changes to the attached legislation and have
the council vote on it in October or November. No action from the council was necessary.
Mr. Greg Sled, Chairman of Cabot Recreation Commission, presented Cabot Parks and
Recreation 2020 Year in Review. Please see attached for a printed copy of the
presentation.
Travis Young, General Manager of Cabot Parks and Rec, addressed the council regarding

WHEREAS, mobile food trucks have experienced a rise in popularity across the country and in the
City of Cabot in the past few years; and

WHEREAS, the City of Cabot finds it desirable to set forth regulations to allow mobile food trucks
to operate within the city under certain circumstances and to establish regulations concerning mobile
food truck operation in order to protect the health safety and welfare of the City's inhabitants.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: Chapter 8, Article II. § 8-18 - Definitions, of the Code of Cabot, is hereby amended to

add the cee definitions:

Mobile Food Establishment - a food establishment or preparing and/or serving foods from a self-
contained vehicle either motorized or within a trailer that is readily movable without disassembling
for transport to another location. Mobile food establishment may serve as a conveyance for
outdoor vending at a fixed location and may be a mobile cart, stationary cart, pedal cart, trailer,
van, portable building, or similar chassis with or without an engine.

Mobile Food Vendor - any person or persons who operate or sell food from a mobile food
establishment.

Mobile Outdoor Vending - exhibiting, displaying, selling or offering for sale any goods, wares
or merchandise from a fixed location on public or private property conveyance.

Mobile Outdoor Vendor - a person that exhibits, displays, sells or offers for sale any goods, wares or
merchandise from a conveyance at a fixed lo cation. This definition does not include a door-to-door
solicitor, mobile food vending, children's lemonade stands or homeowners having garage sales.

Fixed Location - a vendor occupying a location for a period of 6 months or less.

Roving Mobile Vendor - a vendor traveling constantly, without a fixed destination.

SECTION 7: Rules and Regulations General.

1. No operator of a mobile food truck shall park, stand, or move a vehicle and conductbusiness within
unauthorized areas of the City;

2 The operator of a mobile food truck is not granted or entitled to the exclusive use of theservice
location, in whole or in part, other than the approved time and place;

3. All mobile food trucks shall offer waste container for public use that the operator shallempty at his

not utilize dumpsters of other existing businesses without the permission of such businesses.

5. No mobile food truck shall make or cause to be made any unreasonable or excessive noise in
violation of City ordinances;

6. A mobile food truck may conduct sales while parked on a public street when the City has approved a
temporary street closure for a City-sponsored or neighborhood-sponsored event such as a street
festival or street fair;

7. Mobile food trucks on public property, the City reserves the right to temporarily move amobile
food truck to a nearby location if the approved location needs to be used for emergency, or other public
purpose.

8. Inspectional Services. The food truck applicant shall ensure compliance with all City and state health
regulations for mobile food truck vendors. Health and Fire inspections will be reciprocated.

9. In no instance, with the exception of special events, may the mobile vendor/ mobile food vendor
reduce the number of available parking spaces below the minimum required for the primary
business.

10. Businesses which require a permit (A&P permit) from the Cabot Advertising and Promotion
Commission (the Commission) in addition to the Cabot City Business License are requiredto obtain
and maintain the A&P permit in good standing as a condition of maintaining the business license.
Revocation of the A&P permit by the Commission shall be deemed to simultaneously revoke the
Cabot City Business License and all business operations shall be required to cease immediately.

SECTION 8: Operation of Mobile Food Trucks.

Operation without A&P Permit or CityBusiness License/Permit.

A mobile food truck, being operated without a valid A & P permit issued by the Cabot Chamber of
Commerce Office, may be cited into Cabot District Court. Any mobile food truck, operating without
a valid City Business License/Permit issued by the City of Cabot Clerk's Office, may be cited into
Cabot District Court.

SECTION 9: Unattended Vehicles Prohibited.

1. No mobile food truck shall be parked on the street overnight, unless present at the location as part of
the mobile food truck event, or left unsecured at any time food is kept in the mobile food truck. Any
mobile food truck which is found to be unsecured shall be considered a public safety hazard and
may be ticketed and impounded.

A mobile food truck operating outside of an approved site, at an unauthorized location, or
beyond the hours for which the operation has been permitted shall be deemed operating in
violationof this section and may be subject to enforcement under this section.

Any person operating a mobile food truck or service, in violation of any provision ofthis section, may
be subject to a fine of three hundred dollars ($300) per day.

The provisions of this Ordinance shall be with the Cabot Code Enforcement Department, Cabot Police
Department, and/or the Cabot Fire Department. If the Code Enforcement Department is not available
to enforce the rules of this Ordinance, enforcement shall be with the Cabot Police Department

SECTION 12: Severability.
In the event any title, section, paragraph, item, sentence, clause, phrase, or word of this ordinance is

the remaining portions of the ordinance, which shall remain in full force and effect as if the portion
so declared or adjudged invalid or unconstitutional were not originally a part of the ordinance.

SECTION 13: Repealer.

All ordinances or resolutions of the City in conflict herewith are hereby repealed to the extent of
such conflict.

SECTION 14: Emergency Clause.

In light of the need for these changes, and the need to provide the residents of the City of Cabot with
dining and other options not associated with brick and mortar locations and commercial facilities, the
Cabot City Council declares that an emergency exists and that the need to provide for the public
peace, health, safety and welfare is necessary, and this Ordinance shall be in full force and effect
from and after the date of its passage and approval.

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on social
distancing by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot moved the
monthly Council Meeting to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508 N. Lincoln, as
advertised. This allowed for spacing between chairs, as suggested. The event
was successfully streamed through YouTube. This meeting may be viewed at
https:/www.youtube.com/watch?v=x_7QelIAo15A.

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the Regular Meeting of the Cabot City
Council at 7:12 p.m. on July 6, 2021 following the regularly scheduled Work
Session. Council Member Matt Webber led the prayer and Council Member
Ron Waymack led the Pledge of Allegiance.

Roll Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present:
James Reid, Matt Webber, Brandon Hillenburg, Ed Long, Ron Waymack,
Michael Jones, Stephen Redd and Maggie Cope. Also in attendance were
Mayor Ken Kincade, City Attorney Ben Hooper, and City Clerk & Treasurer
Tammy Yocom.

Mayor Kincade presented a Mayoral Proclamation to Eagle Scout recipient
Samuel Rogers.

Approval of Minutes from Last Meeting and Other Matters

Motion to read legislation by title only by Mr. Jones, second by Mr. Redd.
Motion passed with a unanimous Roll Call Vote.

ORDINANCE NO. 23 OF 2021

AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND SECTIONS OF THE CODE OF CABOT; DECLARING AN
EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the 93" General Assembly of the State of Arkansas adopted Act 435 which
made certain changes to county and municipal procurement law and increased the expenditure
amount for when competitive bidding must be used; and

WHEREAS, there are certain provisions of the Code of Cabot that need to be amended in
order to be consistent with the new provisions of state law enacted by Act 435; and

WHEREAS, The Cabot City Council desires that city code be consistent with state law
and it is amended herein;

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS:

SECTION 1: Code of Cabot Sec. 2-578, Sec. 2-579, Sec. 2-580 are hereby amended
consistent with the attached Exhibit A.

SECTION 2: Any municipal legislation or portion of municipal legislation in conflict
with this ordinance is hereby repealed.

SECTION 3: If any provision of this Ordinance or the application thereof is held invalid,
such invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of the Ordinance which can be
given effect without the invalid provisions or application, and to this end, the provisions of this
Ordinance are declared to be severable.

SECTION 4: The operation of city government and the necessary and essential services it
provides to the public depend on city code being an accurate statement of the law and in
compliance with state law so as not to create conflicting legal provisions. It is therefore essential to
the health, welfare, and safety of the general public that city code be consistent with and comply
with state law as it is currently enacted. An emergency is therefore declared and this ordinance
and the code amendments authorized herein will go into effect alongside Act 435 on July 28, 2021.

presented. The previous board did not file with the IRS and this jeopardized the 501 C3 status.

positions and will meet again tomorrow night. General Director Travis Young asked the current
board to reach out to him and he will assist them with the issues. Communication with the
Cabot Youth Cheer has been difficult. The Association contract was not signed until March
which delayed the current board from obtaining the information needed to begin their duties.

season will go on as planned.

the park department send some of the maintenance workers to assist with the track. Soil tack
will be purchased to help with the dirt. General Director Travis Young stated he can send help
for them.

currently in season. Early bird registration, with good discounts, are being held for all youth
sports. Fall baseball and softball registration includes a shirt and hat this year. Youth soccer will
hold tryouts for 10U and up.

Making sure all voters have the correct information is the top priority. Placing signs out in the
city and getting brochures out is currently being done. Staff is permitted to tell the public about
the bond items, including on social media. The key is to educate the citizens, especially those
that use the parks, and to get them to vote. A Town Hall meeting is set for tomorrow night at
Magness Creek Elementary and the 29th at Central Elementary.

None

The 4th of July went well but attendance was down due to competing with surrounding area
displays. Next year we will consider a different date so that Cabot will be one of the first
fireworks displays to attend. We are seeking out a grant to allow us to be a sight for electric
cars to plug in at the community center. French drains have been installed at the sports fields.
Fall sports schedules have been completed. Top dressing with sand is being done. The
pickleball court bid came in at $76,000.00. Travis Young is working to reconfigure the bid using
asphalt to reduce the cost. The goal is to have the project complete by October.

Halff Associates, Inc. (“Halff’) will perform professional design services for the City of

south of Locust to line up with the Vine Street intersection. The design will also include
curb and gutter, curb inlets, underground culverts, and detail measures to improve the
storm water conveyance along this section of roadway. The plans will include construction
budget estimates for the project for use by the City in establishing phasing priorities and
financial planning of the proposed improvements.

of Cabot.

ORDINANCE 24 OF 2021
AN ORDINANCE TO PERMIT COUNCIL MEMBERS, OFFICIALS, AND/OR
MUNICIPAL EMPLOYEES TO DO BUSINESS WITH THE CITY OF CABOT;
DECLARING AN EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
WHEREAS, Ark. Code Ann § 14-42-107(b)(1) states that no alderman, council member,
official, or municipal employee shall be interested, directly or indirectly, in the profit of any
contract for furnishing supplies, equipment, or services to the municipality unless the governing
body of the City has enacted an ordinance specifically permitting alderman, council members,
officials, or municipal employees to conduct business with the City; and
WHEREAS, the City is need of renovation work to the front facade, stairway, and ramp
of City Hall. After complying with city code in regards to procuring services under $35,000, the
City desires to retain Wittenberg, Delony & Davidson, Inc. to preform architectural services for
the project; and
WHEREAS, Chad Young is the president and CEO for Wittenberg, Delony & Davidson,
Inc. and he is also a commissioner with the Cabot Planning Commission. The City Council
must therefore grant its permission via ordinance in order for the City to utilize Wittenberg,
Delony & Davidson, Inc. to provide architectural services for this project.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: Chad Young, and by extension Wittenberg, Delony & Davidson, Inc., is
hereby permitted to conduct business with the City of Cabot, Arkansas by providing architectural
and related services for renovation of the front fagade, stairway, and ramp of City Hall. The
authorized services are to be consistent with the attached Exhibit A.

SECTION 2: Cabot City Hall sees numerous members of the public and employees pass
through on a daily basis. The condition of the front fagade, stairway, and stairs has become
substantially degraded so as to constitute a potential hazard if renovations are not promptly
conducted. An emergency is therefore declared, and this ordinance, being necessary for the
preservation of the public peace, health, safety, and welfare, shall be in full force and effect from

and after its passage.

ARTICLE 6 COST OF THE WORK

§ 6.1 For purposes of this Agreement, the Cost of the Work shall be the total cost to the Owner to construct all
elements of the Project designed or specified by the Architect and shall include contractors’ general conditions costs,
ovethead and profit. The Cost of the Work also includes the reasonable value of labor, materials, and equipment,
donated to, or otherwise furnished by, the Owner. The Cost of the Work does not include the compensation of the
Architect; the costs of the land, rights-of-way, financing, or contingencies for changes in the Work; or other costs that
are the responsibility of the Owner.

§ 6.2 The Owner’s budget for the Cost of the Work is provided in Initial Information, and shall be adjusted throughout
the Project as required under Sections 5.2, 6.4 and 6.5. Evaluations of the Owner’s budget for the Cost of the Work,
and the preliminary estimate of the Cost of the Work and updated estimates of the Cost of the Work, prepared by the
Architect, represent the Architect’s judgment as a design professional. It is recognized, however, that neither the
Architect nor the Owner has control over the cost of labor, materials, or equipment; the Contractor’s methods of
determining bid prices; or competitive bidding, market, or negotiating conditions. Accordingly, the Architect cannot
and does not warrant or represent that bids or negotiated prices will not vary from the Owner’s budget for the Cost of
the Work, or from any estimate of the Cost of the Work, or evaluation, prepared or agreed to by the Architect.

§ 6.3 In preparing estimates of the Cost of Work, the Architect shall be permitted to include contingencies for design,
bidding, and price escalation; to determine what materials, equipment, component systems, and types of construction
are to be included in the Contract Documents; to recommend reasonable adjustments in the program and scope of the
Project; and to include design alternates as may be necessary to adjust the estimated Cost of the Work to meet the
Owner’s budget. The Architect’s estimate of the Cost of the Work shall be based on current area, volume or similar
conceptual estimating techniques. If the Owner requires a detailed estimate of the Cost of the Work, the Architect shall
provide such an estimate, if identified as the Architect's responsibility in Section 4.1.1, as a Supplemental Service.

Section 4.8. - Site Plan Review-Current Code

4.8.1 General Purpose and Review Guidelines.
The purpose of this section is to set forth procedure for processing site plans and to establish
standards for development within those districts which require regulation by this section.

Site Plan Review is a development review process that provides for case-by-case consideration
of project particulars including the provision of parking and landscaping, siting of buildings, and
the compatibility of the proposed development with adjacent uses. Stand-alone Parking Lots
shall be considered "developments" and will be reviewed in the same manner in which all Site
Plans are reviewed.

All development shall be designed in such a way as to minimize any potential deleterious impact
on the surrounding area. Special attention shall be given to buffering commercial developments
from adjacent single-family areas. Design of the internal street system ingress and egress, off-
street parking, loading and pedestrian ways shall be sensitive to such conditions as safety,
convenience, separation of vehicular and pedestrian traffic, general attractiveness, areas of
dwelling units, and the proper relationship of different land uses. Landscaped areas shall be
provided to reduce erosion, heat and glare, and said areas shall be maintained in an attractive
condition. Existing trees on a development site shall be retained where possible. Screening, open
space, or other buffer may be required to give adequate separation between uses which are not
compatible and shall also be provided for the beautification and enhancement of the property.
The requirements of Arkansas State Fire Code, Section 508, providing for handicapped parking
and accessibility shall be indicated on the plan.

4.8.2 Applicable Districts.

Any application for a zoning classification which involves Site Plan review may be initiated by
the owner or other person having a contractual interest in the property for which Site Plan
approval is requested or by the authorized agent of such owner or person. The Site Plan review
process shall apply to all applications for the following zoning districts:

"O-1" Office and Quiet Business District.
"C-1" Central Business District

"C-2" General Commercial District.
"C-3" Open Display Commercial District.

"I-1" Industrial District

4.8.3 Procedure and Authority.

The procedure for the zoning of property to one of the above three classifications shall be the
same as for any other zoning application. The Planning Commission may outline special
parameters or special concerns which will apply to the Site Plan when such are identified through
the zoning process.

The Site Plan Review process occurs when a building permit is requested. The Building
Inspector and the Planning Commission shall review Site Plans prior to the issuance of a building
permit. At that time, the plan will be assessed for compatibility with standards and criteria
provided herein. Review of a Site Plan proposal shall take place at regularly scheduled monthly
meetings at which time interested persons may appear and offer information in support of or
against the proposed Site Plan. The Administrative Official will make recommendations to the
full Planning Commission at said public meeting and said Commission will then take one of the
following steps: approve the Site Plan as submitted; approve the Site Plan with modifications;
defer the Site Plan for future review; or deny the Site Plan.

In addition to the special requirements of this section, the Planning Commission may impose on
a Site Plan such additional requirements as are necessary to safeguard the public health, safety
and general welfare. The Planning Commission may require the Applicant to submit a revised
Site Plan incorporating the imposed requirements and modifications. Such revised Site Plans
shall have priority over new applications in the review process. The Planning commission may
deny a Site Plan and recommend reducing the zoning classification of any parcel which requires
a Site Plan if it does not carry out the general purpose of this section. In those instances where a
variance from district standards is requested as a part of the submittal request, the Planning
Commission may modify or waive standards. A variance may be allowed only after
demonstration of a hardship unique to the development proposal filed. Pecuniary difficulties
shall not be deemed to constitute a hardship.

Site plans will be reviewed by the Planning Commission under the following circumstances. All
other Site Plans shall be considered minor Site Plans and shall be reviewed by the staff.

a. Buildings or developments placed on a plot of real property of two acres or larger.

b. Any development containing a building with a combined square footage of 10,000 square
feet or more.

c. All multi-family housing developments containing twenty or more units.

d. Any building or development storing, using or selling petroleum products, flammable
products or hazardous materials.

e. Any project referred by the City Staff.

4.8.5 Standards for Site Plan Disapproval.
The Planning Commission shall not disapprove an application for a Site Plan except on the basis
of findings directed to one or more specified particular of the following standards:

a. The proposed Site Plan is incomplete or contains or reveals violations of this Code or
applicable district regulations which the Applicant has, after written request, failed or
refused to supply or correct.

b. The proposed Site Plan interferes unnecessarily with easements, roadways, rail lines,
utilities, and other public or private rights-of-way.

c. The proposed pedestrian and vehicular circulation systems incorporated in the Site Plan
subsequently create hazards to safety on or off the site.

d. The proposed Site Plan does not conform to the minimum drainage requirements found
in the Subdivision and Development Code or other applicable ordinances.

e. The proposed Site Plan violates the basic intent of this Code or does not comply with
those conditions which were stipulated at the time of rezoning.

4.8.6 Effect of Approval.

An approved Site Plan shall be binding on the Applicants and their successors and assignees. No
building permit shall be issued for any building or structure not in conformance with the Site
Plan. The construction, location, use, or operation of all land and structures within the Site Plan
shall be in accordance with all conditions and limitations set forth in the Site Plan. No structure,
use or other element of an approved Site Plan shall be eliminated, altered or provided in another
manner unless an amendment is approved in accordance with this section; provided, however,
that the Building Inspector may approve such minor changes in the Site Plan as will not cause
any of the following circumstances to occur:

a. Any change in the allowable use of the development.

b. An increase of greater than five percent in the number of dwelling units, but not to exceed
the total allowable dwelling units in the respective zoning classification.

c. Any modification compounding the problems of vehicular circulation, safety, and
provision of public utilities.

d. Any modification having an adverse impact on adjacent property.

e. Any reduction of the off-street parking and loading requirements below those specified
in this Code.

f. Any change in the allowable size, lighting, or orientation of signs.

Whenever the individual responsible for the reviewing building permits finds that any proposed
construction or occupancy will not, in their opinion, comply with the approved Site Plan, they
shall refer the question to the Planning Commission for review.

4.8.7 Amendments.
The holder of an approved Site Plan may request modification of the Site Plan or the conditions
of approval by submitting an amended Site Plan which shall be filed and processed in the same

manner as the original application.

4.8.8 Appeals.

Any Applicant aggrieved by a decision of the Planning Commission as it relates to the Site Plan
review process shall have the right to appeal to the City Council. Said appeal shall be filed in
writing with the City Clerk-Treasurer within thirty days of the Planning Commission decision.
Such appeal must state the reasons for disagreement with the decision of the Planning
Commission.

4.8.5 Standards for Site Plan Disapproval.
The Planning Commission shall not disapprove an application for a Site Plan except on the basis
of findings directed to one or more specified particular of the following standards:

a. The proposed Site Plan is incomplete or contains or reveals violations of this Code or
applicable district regulations which the Applicant has, after written request, failed or
refused to supply or correct.

b. The proposed Site Plan interferes unnecessarily with easements, roadways, rail lines,
utilities, and other public or private rights-of-way.

c. The proposed pedestrian and vehicular circulation systems incorporated in the Site Plan
subsequently create hazards to safety on or off the site.

d. The proposed Site Plan does not conform to the minimum drainage requirements found
in the Subdivision and Development Code or other applicable ordinances.

e. The proposed Site Plan violates the basic intent of this Code or does not comply with
those conditions which were stipulated at the time of rezoning.

4.8.6 Effect of Approval.
An approved Site Plan shall be binding on the Applicants and their successors and assignees. No
building permit shall be issued for any building or structure not in conformance with the Site
Plan. The construction, location, use, or operation of all land and structures within the Site Plan
shall be in accordance with all conditions and limitations set forth in the Site Plan. No structure,
use or other element of an approved Site Plan shall be eliminated, altered or provided in another
manner unless an amendment is approved in accordance with this section; provided, however,
that the Building Inspector may approve such minor changes in the Site Plan as will not cause
any of the following circumstances to occur:
a. Any change in the allowable use of the development.
b. An increase of greater than five percent in the number of dwelling units, but not to exceed
the total allowable dwelling units in the respective zoning classification.
c. Any modification compounding the problems of vehicular circulation, safety, and
provision of public utilities.
d. Any modification having an adverse impact on adjacent property.
e. Any reduction of the off-street parking and loading requirements below those specified
in this Code.
f. Any change in the allowable size, lighting, or orientation of signs.

§ 3.2.1 The Architect shall review the program and other information furnished by the Owner, and shall review laws,

§ 3.2.3 The Architect shall present its preliminary evaluation to the Owner and shall discuss with the Owner
alternative approaches to design and construction of the Project. The Architect shall reach an understanding with the
Owner regarding the requirements of the Project.

§ 3.2.4 Based on the Project requirements agreed upon with the Owner, the Architect shall prepare and present, for the
Owner’s approval, a preliminary design illustrating the scale and relationship of the Project components.

§ 3.2.5 Based on the Owner’s approval of the preliminary design, the Architect shall prepare Schematic Design
Documents for the Owner’s approval. The Schematic Design Documents shall consist of drawings and other
documents including a site plan, if appropriate, and preliminary building plans, sections and elevations; and may
include some combination of study models, perspective sketches, or digital representations. Preliminary selections of
major building systems and construction materials shall be noted on the drawings or described in writing.

orientation, together with other considerations based on program and aesthetics, in developing a design that is
consistent with the Owner’s program, schedule and budget for the Cost of the Work. The Owner may obtain more
advanced sustainable design services as a Supplemental Service under Section 4.1.1.

§ 3.2.5.2 The Architect shall consider the value of alternative materials, building systems and equipment, together
with other considerations based on program and aesthetics, in developing a design for the Project that is consistent
with the Owner’s program, schedule, and budget for the Cost of the Work.

§ 3.2.6 The Architect shall submit to the Owner an estimate of the Cost of the Work prepared in accordance with

§ 3.2.7 The Architect shall submit the Schematic Design Documents to the Owner, and request the Owner’s approval.

Most of the county’s flooding and drainage problems are found in communities in the less hilly areas,
such as Allport, Austin, Cabot, and Carlisle. Flash floods are most common in this area due to this
area exhibiting high to moderate relief, steep to moderate slopes, and bedrock with low permeability.
All factors facilitate rapid runoff and the consequent potential for flash floods. Urban development in
this partof the county exacerbates the flash flooding problem. Intense rainfall events, often
accompanying the large thunderstorms that occur in Lonoke County several times a year, have
resulted in water flowing rapidly into lower areas, collecting in, and sometimes overtopping the valley
streams.

The Union Pacific Railroad runs through the City of Cabot and most of the drainage in the City flows
to the ditches along each side of the existing railroad. This project would widen and dredge the
existing ditches on each side of the railroad for its entire route within the city limits. This project
would also dredge the existing tributaries and ditches that flow into the railroad ditches.

Cabot City Council Work Session
Veterans Park Event Center
September 7, 2021
6:30 p.m.

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on social distancing
by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot moved the monthly Work Session
to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508 N. Lincoln, as advertised. This allowed for spacing
between chairs, as suggested. The event was successfully streamed through YouTube.

You may view this meeting @ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9zgTilGWxG4&t= 10s.

Council members present were: Ed Long, Brandon Hillenburg, James Reid, Matt Webber,
Ron Waymack and Stephen Redd. Michael Jones was absent. Maggie Cope joined the
meeting at 6:53 pm. Others present: Mayor Ken Kincade, City Attorney Ben Hooper, and
City Clerk & Treasurer Tammy Yocom.

Mayor Kincade opened the meeting at 6:30 p.m.

Municipal Services Committee Business: (Members are: Long, Reid, Redd & Cope)
1. An Ordinance to Permit Council Members, Officials, and/or Municipal Employees to Do
Business with the City Of Cabot — Presented By Ben Hooper. This is a “housekeeping”
issue allowing Chad Young, who is Chairman of the Planning Commission, to do business
with the City. This legislation has nothing to do with the contract that will come at a later
date. Motion by James Reid to place this item on the next Council Meeting, second by
Ed Long. Motion passed 3-0.

2. An Ordinance Creating, Certifying, And Confirming Tax Liens Against Real Properties
At Various Locations Within The City Of Cabot - Presented By Laura Nobles. Motion by
James Reid to place this item on the next Council Meeting, second by Stephen Redd.
Motion passed 3-0.

3. An Ordinance Providing For the Redistricting Of Wards for the City Of Cabot - Presented
By Mayor Ken Kincade. City Attorney Ben Hooper explained with the new Census data
out it is a good time to look into redistricting of Wards, but it is not necessary since the
council is voted on at large. Redistricting is referenced in the code as needing to be
discussed which is being accomplished tonight. Wards can be left alone, changed or
changed at a later date. Ben suggested voting the legislation down if you want to keep
the wards the same and not tabling it for an indefinite time. Should the council wish to
address this at a later date, it can be done with a separate ordinance. Discussion. Motion
to move this item to the next Council Meeting by James Reid, second by Stephen Redd.
Motion passed 3-0.

4. A Resolution Authorizing The Mayor and City-Clerk / Treasurer To Grant American
Rescue Plan Act Funds To The Cabot Water And Wastewater Commission For Use In
Permissible Projects — Presented By Mayor Ken Kincade. Brian Boroughs is working with
Cabot WaterWorks on a sewer expansion. The legislation in the packet is a result of
refining from both Ben Hooper and the attorney for the Water Commission. Ed Long
stated he had a conversation with Gary Walker, Chairman of the Water Commission,
before this meeting and the Commission is fine with it. Motion to send this item to the
next Council Meeting by James Reid, second by Stephen Redd. Motion passed 3-0.

--- page 2 (OCR) ---
5. A Resolution Authorizing The Submittal Of An Application For BRIC Grant Funds To The
State Of Arkansas And The Federal Government — Presented By Brian Boroughs. This is
a notice of intent for a Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities Grant. At this
time, we are only showing our interest and hoping to be invited to apply. Discussion.
Motion to send this item to the next Council Meeting by Stephen Redd, second by James
Reid. Motion passed 4-0 (Maggie Cope joined the meeting).

6. Municipal Services Community Input-None

Budget & Personnel Committee Business: (Members are: Webber, Hillenburg, &
Jones).1. A Resolution Adopting Premium Pay For Certain City Employees From The
American Rescue Plan — Presented By Matthew Hood. ARPA allows us to provide Premium
Pay to employees directly working in the community and around COVID, After speaking
with other cities in the area regarding the benefit they are providing to their employees
as reference, it was determined a onetime bonus to eligible employees would be paid out
with a portion of these funds. Motion to move this item to the next Council Meeting by
Brandon Hillenburg, second by Matt Webber. Motion passed 2-0.

2. Budget & Personnel Community Input-None

Police & Fire Committee Business: (Members are: Reid, Hillenburg, Redd & Cope)
1. A Resolution Approving a Change Order for the Refurbishment of Engine 1 for the
Cabot Fire Department — Presented By Chief Dwayne Boswell. As expected, once work
began on Engine 1, a list of 25 items totaling over $28,000 was found that needed repair.
They have also requested a blackout trim kit for an additional $15,500 which will match
the new rescue squad that will be purchased by 2021 bond proceeds. Discussion. Motion
to move this item to the next council meeting by Stephen Redd, second by Brandon
Hillenburg. Motion passed 4-0

2. Police & Fire Committee Input-None

Community Development Committee Business: (Members are: Long & Reid)

1. Community Development Input - None

Military Affairs Committee Business: (Members are: Waymack, Jones & Webber)

1. Military Affairs Input-None
