Cabot Parks and Recreation Commission Regular Meeting
August 17, 2021, at 6:30pm
Veterans Park Community Center
508 North Lincoln, Cabot, Arkansas 72023

I.

Call to Order/Roll Call
Greg Sled called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm.
Present: Greg Sled, John Rudd, Ashley Little, Tricia Ambeau, Tricia Ambeau
Guest: Attorney Greg Crumpton

II.

Minutes of Regular Meeting
Minutes from the meeting held on July 20, 2021, were presented. JOHN RUDD MOTIONED TO
ACCEPT THE MINUTES OF JULY 20, 2021, SECOND BY SHELIA DEARMOND. ALL SAY AYE.

III.

Financials
General Director Travis Young presented the July 2021 financials. JOHN RUDD MOTIONED TO
APPROVE THE JULY 2021 FINANCIALS, SECOND BY ASHLEY LITTLE. Insurance came out of the
budget a month early. Fall registration income numbers are good. The turf maintenance
contract was discussed as army worms have been a huge problem and funds had to be spent
for pest control. The air conditioner units in several buildings, including the community center,
need repair. Cost of concession supplies are up. There are some supplies in back stock that will
transfer to football concessions this fall. The outdoor pickleball courts were discussed and will
require sealing the asphalt. ALL SAY AYE.

IV.

Programs
Cabot Youth Football Association presented their report. Registration is going well with 145
already registered. Bank account looks good, and the draft will be held this Saturday.
Flag Football – Registration is doing well, and the draft is scheduled for this Saturday.
BMX – Racing made it through this past weekend before the rain came and the track had to be
redone. Forty-nine riders raced on Saturday and 47 riders on Sunday. Out of state riders did
not come due to the weather. A new rider training session will be held on September 2nd and
run through November 1st.
Cabot Youth Cheer – no report, registration was scheduled for this evening.
Program Director Lorenzo Mendoza gave the parks department program report. There are
close to one thousand children registered for fall sports to date. The coaches meeting will be
held next week. Soccer age divisions was discussed with some changes made to the age groups

85

this year. Most practices will begin the week of August 30th and games will begin on September
13th. Volleyball is scheduled to begin on Sept. 25th.
V.

Old Business
Bond – General Director Travis Young stated that he would like to do something extra as a
thank you for all those involved in making the election successful. He asked the commission
for any suggestion. John Rudd suggested that this be a day-to-day issue and trust that the right
decision will be made. Mr. Young discussed the bond items in more detail. The City of Cabot
will take over the community pavilion. The choices available for land purchase include the 321
Sports Complex, which will need a second entrance; property off Willie Ray Road; Hwy 5 and 89
interchange; or the property on highway 89 between Firestone Restaurant and the future
Atwood’s store. The City of Cabot will address these properties depending on who is willing to
sell. The Bond financing will be done by November 17th. The goal of this department is to have
all projects completed by January 2023. The parks commission will have the final vote as to the
location to purchase. The City of Cabot has hired Brian Boroughs as the Special Projects Director
and he will help with our projects as well. How the money will be allocated for each facility was
discussed including land acquisitions and utilities. Mr. Young was asked which land he favored.
He stated that the land off Willie Ray, which is the new 3rd Cabot exit, would be ideal because of
potential new growth in that area with Unity Health ready to build. Greg Sled stated that a
construction committee will be formed soon to oversee the projects.

VI.

New Business
Staffing – Looking at hiring a Human Resource Manage was discussed. Using a third party or
hiring inhouse was discussed. Trisha Ambeau opened discussion on the need of full-time verse
part-time duties for the position. The commission asked that Mr. Young advertise for part-time
and see what happens.
Assistant Aquatic Supervisor – Mr. Young stated that the need for additional aquatic staff was
necessary to operate the Aquatic Park and indoor pool, along with all aquatic programs within
the department, efficiently. Revenue is being lost due to lack of supervision over swim lessons.
This would be an entry level job with a salary starting at around $30,000.00 annually. Other
duties could be assigned to fill gaps during down times. Mr. Young will send out the Municipal
Leagues surveys on salaries via email to all commissioners.
Turf Contract – The original proposal for the turf was $784,400.00 but the figures are now
$818,080.00. The company is currently working with Cabot Schools and will move over to our
project as soon as they complete the schools’ project. Mr. Young asked to move forward

86

immediately so that our project can be done by the end of Fall. Attorney Greg Crumpton sees
no issue with the contract regarding beginning before the bond money has been received. The
department will not be held to the contract if something happens to delay the bond. TRICIA
AMBEAU MOTIONED TO APPROVE ENTERING INTO CONTRACT WITH DEAL SERVICES AND
GIVE MR. YOUNG AUTHORITY TO PROCEED WITH THE TURF INSTALLATION, SECOND BY
ASHLEY LITTLE, ALL SAY AYE.
Playground/Splash Pad/Restroom Contract – Mr. Young discussed the companies that specialize
in all-inclusive playground structures. The quote received by Hahn Recreation came in at
$899,843.67. This company can do the entire project. JOHN RUDD MOTIONED TO ACCEPT THE
CONTRACT, CONTINGENT THAT THE COST OF BUILDING MATERIALS ARE COVERED UNDER
THE CURRENT INSURANCE POLICY IF ANY DAMAGE IS DONE BEFORE INSTALLATION, IN THE
AMOUNT OF $899,843.67, SECOND BY TRICIA AMBEAU, ALL SAY AYE.
Community Center Age Policy – The ages to allow children to enter without an adult was
discussed. The policy will remain as is with no changes. Space at the community center will be
opened up once the sports facilities are built allowing for more activities to be offered.
VII.

Construction/Directors Report
Mr. Young discussed the materials needed for the BMX track.
Community Center Director interviews are being held with those selected from eighteen
applicants.
Mr. Young asked the commission members to attend the upcoming youth sports coaches’
meetings if possible.

VIII.

Subcommittee Reports
None

IX.

Community Input
Mr. Young stated that the next Recreation Grant is coming soon and would like to build a
skateboard park next to the BMX track. Pump track may be possible soon. Mr. Young stated
that staff will attend a Bike School, which the City of Cabot is funding, on bike trail development
and how to integrate trails in the community. Staff will be attending several programs for
continued education as the parks evolve.
Next meeting will be held on September 21, 2021.

87

IX.

Adjournment
ASHLEY LITTLE MOTIONED TO ADJOURN AT 7:49 PM, SECOND BY JOHN RUDD. ALL SAY AYE.

CERTIFICATE
I, the undersigned Chairman, do hereby certify the foregoing to be a true and accurate record of the
proceedings of the regular meeting of the Parks and Recreation August 17, 2021.
______________________________ __________________
Parks and Recreation Commission Chairman

Motion to approve the $2,000 was made by Greg Jones

AGENDA ITEMS
In response to the 2020 COVID-19 outbreak and restrictions placed on
social distancing by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot
moved the monthly Planning Commission Meeting to the Veterans Park
Event Center, 508 North Lincoln. This allowed for ten feet of spacing
between chairs as suggested. The meeting was both open to the public
and an online meeting with video through the web-based video
conferencing tool Zoom.
1. Call to Order
Chairman Young called to order the regular meeting of the Cabot
Planning Commission at 7:00 PM, at the Veterans Park Event Center.
Opening prayer and the Pledge of Allegiance were led by Chairman
Young.
2. Roll Call
A roll call was conducted. The following persons were present:
Commission members Liz Bird, Chuck Prater, Mitch Ward, Jim Knaack,
Matt Moudy, Ronny Loe, Chairman Young and City Attorney Ben Hooper
attending via Zoom were Halff – City Engineer Brian Vines and Garver –
City Planner Courtney McNair.
3. Approval of Minutes from Last Meeting and Other Matters
The minutes of the July 2021 Regular Planning Commission meeting
were approved with a motion by Mr. Prater and a second by Mr. Ward,
Motion passed unanimously by a Roll Call Vote 6-0-0.
4. Planning Commission (Public Hearing)
a) Amendments to the Unified Development Code – (Laura Nobles)
Section 4.8. – Site Plan Review –Motion to approve as submitted by
Mr. Prater, second by Mr. Loe. Motion passed unanimously by Roll
Call Vote 6-0-0. This item will be passed to council.
Section 5.3. – Subdivision Requirements – Motion to approve as
submitted by Mr. Loe, Second by Mr. Ward. Motion passed
unanimously by Roll Call Vote 6-0-0. This item will be passed to
council.
Section 4.10.2.b.iii – Driveways Width– Councilman Hillenburg
presented revised code suggestions. After a brief discussion Motion to
approve changes as discussed by Mr. Moudy, Second by Mr. Ward,
Motion passed by a Roll Call Vote
5-1-0, with Mr. Loe voting No. This
95
item will be passed to council.

Section 5.4.8.b.ii – Driveway Approach – After a brief discussion, A
Motion to approve by Prater, Second by Mr. Moudy. Motion passed by
a Roll Call Vote 5-1-0, with Mr. Loe voting No. This item will be
passed to council.
Land Use Fee Schedule – Motion to approve as discussed by Mr.
Knaack, Second by Mr. Moudy. Motion passed by a Roll Call Vote 5-10, with Mr. Ward voting No. This item will be passed to council.
5. Planning Commission (New Business)
a) Final Plat – Reserve at the Pines, Phase I – (Lemons Engineering)
After a discussion, a Motion to approve with contingencies by Mr. Loe,
second by Mr. Prater, motion was approved unanimously by Roll Call
Vote, 6-0-0 with the following contingencies: The certificate of
Engineering Accuracy must be signed and dated; The certificate of
Surveying Accuracy must be signed and dated; Hwy 89/South Pine
Street is a Principal Arterial Street. Right-of-way width is 90 feet.
Dedication shall be 45 feet from the centerline of the road. Revise the
nomenclature of the ROW to 90 feet and not 80 feet; The North inlet
pipe stub still needs permanent repairs; the fire hydrant at the front
of the property needs to be raised to the finish grade.
6.

Adjournment
There being no further business to come before the Planning
Commission, the meeting was adjourned at 7:58 p.m.
